value: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン (Shin Seiki Evangerion)

value: Gainax and Tatsunoko Production (studios), Hideaki Anno (director)

excerpt: a Japanese anime television series produced by Gainax and Tatsunoko Production, and directed by Hideaki Anno

value: One season, 26 episodes on TV Tokyo, October 4, 1995 to March 27, 1996
text: Evangelion aired as a single season of 26 episodes on TV Tokyo, starting on October 4, 1995 and finishing on March 27, 1996.
excerpt: It began broadcasting in Japan on TV Tokyo on October 4, 1995, and ended on March 27, 1996.

value: Tokyo-3 in 2015

value: A Cruel Angel's Thesis - Yoko Takahashi

value: Development began in 1993 under Hideaki Anno
text: Hideaki Anno began shaping the project in 1993, after a depression that followed his earlier work, with the idea of a hero who stops running away.
excerpt: Anno began the development of the new series in 1993 around the notion of not running away

value: Anime Grand Prix, Best Loved Series: first place in 1996 and 1997
text: Animage readers voted Evangelion their top Best Loved Series at the Anime Grand Prix in 1996, and again in 1997.
excerpt: In 1996, the series won first place in the "Best Loved Series" category of the Anime Grand Prix, a reader-polled award series published in Animage magazine.

value: Netflix worldwide premiere on June 21, 2019
text: Netflix brought the series to a global audience from June 21, 2019, but outside Japan the closing song Fly Me to the Moon is left out for licensing reasons.
excerpt: On March 22, 2019, Netflix announced a June 21, 2019, premiere date for the titles.
